summary.text: The question requires verification from UNESCO, Britannica, or scholarly sources ONLY. I must label each as VERIFIED or UNCERTAIN with exact source URL.

action.query: Borobudur "Kamadhatu" OR "Rupadhatu" OR "Arupadhatu" scholarly OR academic OR UNESCO OR Britannica
Borobudur Karmawibhangga panels OR reliefs site:whc.unesco.org OR britannica.com
Borobudur "1,460" OR "1460" OR "2,672" OR stupas OR Buddha statues Britannica OR UNESCO

content.text:
**VERIFIED (with sources below):** 

(1) Yes. UNESCO explicitly states: "the *kamadhatu* is represented by the base, the *rupadhatu* by the five square terraces, and the *arupadhatu* by the three circular platforms as well as the big stupa." It frames this as the Buddhist cosmological division into spheres of desires, forms, and formlessness, blended with ancestor worship and the path to Nirvana. Britannica describes the same three-level symbolism (*kama-dhatu* lowest/realm of feeling with earthly desires; *rupa-dhatu* middle/realm of form; *arupa-dhatu* upper/realm of formlessness), the mandala form (square as earth, circle as heaven), and the overall structure as combining stupa, temple-mountain, and mandala.[[1]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/)[[2]](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Borobudur)

(2) **UNCERTAIN** on exact panel count (sources say "hundreds" without a precise number). The hidden/encased base (partially or fully concealed by a later-added foot/platform) carries the Karmawibhangga relief series illustrating earthly desires/*kama-dhatu*. Britannica notes "hundreds of reliefs of earthly desires" at the lowest, partially hidden level. UNESCO does not detail the Karmawibhangga series or panel count.[[2]](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Borobudur)

(3) **VERIFIED**: 72 perforated/openwork (bell-shaped) stupas on the three circular terraces, each originally containing a Buddha statue (many still do, visible through perforations). UNESCO: "Around the circular platforms are 72 openwork stupas, each containing a statue of the Buddha." Britannica: "lining the terraces are 72 bell-shaped stupas, many still containing a statue of the Buddha, partly visible through the perforated stonework." Total Buddha statues on the monument are not specified in these sources (only the 72 are quantified here).[[1]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/)[[2]](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Borobudur)

(4) **UNCERTAIN**. These sources do not confirm 1,460 narrative panels on the six square terraces or provide a total relief panel count (including decorative). UNESCO notes reliefs covering ~2,500–2,520 m² total surface area on walls/balustrades but gives no panel counts or breakdown. Britannica mentions series of reliefs on the levels without numbers.[[1]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/)

(5) No. Both UNESCO and Britannica describe **five** concentric square terraces (as the *rupadhatu*/body/middle level), plus a pyramidal/square base (the hidden *kamadhatu* foot) and three circular platforms/terraces above—totaling nine lesser sections/levels in effect. There is no discrepancy in these authoritative sources; any reference to "six" square terraces appears to be a non-authoritative counting variation (e.g., treating the base as an additional square level) not supported here.[[1]](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/592/)[[2]](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Borobudur)

(6) **VERIFIED** for clockwise (*pradakshina*); upward is implied by the structure. Britannica states: "a pilgrim begins at the eastern stairway and walks clockwise around each of the monument’s nine levels before reaching the top." This aligns with the standard Buddhist *pradakshina* circumambulation. UNESCO does not specify direction but describes the vertical progression through the tiers toward Nirvana/enlightenment.[[2]](https://www.britannica.com/topic/Borobudur)

All statements above draw **only** from the cited UNESCO World Heritage Centre page and Britannica entries (no other sources used). Some numerical details (e.g., exact relief panels) are absent from these sources and thus marked UNCERTAIN.
